summary: loom's claim checker verifies that every path a stage names in filesCreated/filesModified/testFilesCreated/testFilesModified actually exists, but has no field for a path a stage removed or renamed away — exactly what happened when saturday-monorepo's golden-site-file-names order renamed seven files and listed them as "old -> new" in filesModified, so the claim check found no such file and parked a correct order as undone work. This feature adds an optional filesDeleted array to ImplementationState and testFilesDeleted to QAState, and adds the opposite-direction claim check to internal/orchestrator/claims.go: a deletion claim passes when the path is absent now and was present when the stage started (observed via the existing posture-check WorkTree's ChangedPaths, which already reports a deleted-tracked-file's old path against the run's base commit — no new WorkTree method is needed). It also rejects "old -> new" written into any single path-naming field across ImplementationState, QAState, and SecurityState, with a message describing the correct two-field encoding.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: implementation.schema.json and qa.schema.json each gain an optional filesDeleted or testFilesDeleted array of paths, generated from the Go structs (never hand-edited), with a description stating that a rename is the new path in filesCreated and the old path in filesDeleted.

A stage that lists a path in filesDeleted passes the claim when the path is absent now and existed when the stage started, observed as the path appearing in the posture check's changed-paths set (which reports status against the run's base commit).
A path in filesDeleted that still exists on disk fails the stage with a ClaimError naming the field and the path: "the file still exists — the stage reported a deletion it did not do".
A path in filesDeleted that never existed (absent now and absent from the posture check's changed-paths set) fails the stage with a ClaimError: "no such file was there to delete".

An entry containing " -> " in any path-naming field (filesCreated, filesModified, filesDeleted, testFilesCreated, testFilesModified, testFilesDeleted, or security's filesModified) fails validation with a message instructing the caller to list the new path in filesCreated and the old path in filesDeleted.
examples: filesModified: ["old-name.go -> new-name.go"] is rejected before claim-checking even runs, at ImplementationState.Validate().
The correct encoding — filesCreated: ["new-name.go"], filesDeleted: ["old-name.go"] — passes both validation and claim-checking.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: requireTouchedFiles counts an implementation that only deletes files as having touched something; it no longer requires filesCreated or filesModified to be non-empty when filesDeleted names at least one path.

An existing state document with no filesDeleted or testFilesDeleted field (the omitempty default) validates exactly as it did before this change — no new required field, no changed behavior for filesCreated/filesModified/testFilesCreated/testFilesModified claims.

Every new or changed function has cyclomatic complexity below 7 (enforced by golangci-lint's gocyclo, already configured at min-complexity 7 in .golangci.yml), every changed line is covered by a test proven able to fail, go test ./... and the lint pass, and no file outside scope.paths (internal/state/**, internal/orchestrator/**, shared/schemas/pipeline/**, docs/features/state-files-deleted/**) changes.

dataModelChanges.description: Add optional filesDeleted array to ImplementationState and optional testFilesDeleted array to QAState. Both are new, omitempty, additive JSON Schema properties — no existing field is removed, renamed, or made required, so every previously-valid document keeps validating unchanged.

architecturalFlags: PathClaim (internal/state/claims.go) gains a second boolean, MustNotExist, alongside the existing MustExist, rather than replacing both with a single tri-state enum (Exists/Deleted/Unchecked). This is a shared data contract consumed by internal/orchestrator/claims.go and by three state types (Implementation, QA, Security); architect should confirm the two-boolean shape (which the existing MustExist doc comment already anticipates: "the flag exists so a future field can opt out explicitly") is preferred over an enum before developer implements it.

The deletion check deliberately reuses the existing WorkTree interface (Digest/ChangedPaths/HeadRef/DiffLinesSince) with no new method: a deleted-but-previously-tracked path already appears in Git's `status --porcelain` output (ChangedPaths()), which is what the executor already calls for posture checking. Extending the WorkTree interface instead would require touching internal/worktree/git.go and internal/factory's test fakes, both outside scope.paths — architect should confirm this no-new-method design is acceptable rather than assuming a richer git-aware check was intended.

Add TestFilesDeleted []string `json:"testFilesDeleted,omitempty"` to QAState (internal/state/qa_state.go) and a {Field: "testFilesDeleted", Paths: q.TestFilesDeleted, MustNotExist: true} entry to QAState.PathClaims() (internal/state/claims.go).

edgeCases.case: A stage lists the same path in both filesCreated and filesDeleted.
edgeCases.handling: Each claim is checked independently — filesCreated requires the path to exist, filesDeleted requires it to be absent — so naming the same path in both always fails one of the two checks, which is the correct outcome for an incoherent claim.

edgeCases.case: Posture checking is disabled for the run (no WorkTree configured, so e.changedPaths() returns nil).
edgeCases.handling: verifyDeletionClaim cannot observe "existed at start" at all in that case, so it only checks that the path is now absent and does not fail the never-existed case. cmd/loom/cmd/run.go always wires a real worktree.Git for production runs, so this gap is limited to reduced test harnesses that deliberately omit WithWorkTree, not real runs.

edgeCases.case: A rename's old path was created and deleted entirely within the same stage, never committed before this run.
edgeCases.handling: git status reports nothing for a path that was never tracked, so it will not appear in ChangedPaths() and the claim fails with "no such file was there to delete" even though the stage's own history disagrees — acceptable per the spec's own "Out of Scope: Git rename detection" line; the stage states what it did and loom checks it against the filesystem and git status, nothing deeper.

edgeCases.case: A path in filesDeleted escapes the project root (e.g. "../../etc/passwd").
edgeCases.handling: resolveWithinRoot already rejects this; existingPaths treats a resolve error the same as "does not exist on disk", so the claim proceeds to the changed-set check, where an escaping path will essentially always fail as unseen — consistent with the existing TestAClaimEscapingTheProjectIsRejected test for the existence direction.
